title: The Sun in HMI continuum light, 10 May 2024 (browse image)

facility.instrument: Helioseismic and Magnetic Imager (HMI), continuum intensitygram
facility.pipeline: SDO browse product HMIIC, 1,024 pixels, orange colour table

credit: Courtesy of NASA/SDO and the AIA, EVE, and HMI science teams

license.statement: SDO data rules (https://sdo.gsfc.nasa.gov/data/rules.php, read 2026-10-24): images and movies are "not copyrighted unless explicitly noted"; credit as above. Browse products are "not intended for science analysis or publication" without the PI's consent, so the pack is display-only.

columns.name: display level
columns.description: 0 to 255, the gray of the colour picture: for the eye, not a measure of light

sidecar.title: The Sun in HMI continuum light, 10 May 2024 (browse image)

history.note: gray of the colour (0.299, 0.587, 0.114): display levels, not light
columns 0 to 1023, rows 0 to 991 from the top left: the bottom 32 rows hold a text label ("SDO/HMI Quick-Look Continuum: 20240510_120000") burned into the picture
row 1 is the bottom, as in FITS

source.archive: SDO, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center (sdo.gsfc.nasa.gov)

citations.text: Pesnell, Thompson and Chamberlin 2012, Solar Physics 275, 3 (SDO)

steps: Decode the JPEG (image-decode.py, Pillow 11.2.1 (libjpeg 6.2)); gray; crop; block mean; rows from the bottom; base64 in the sidecar. Each step is in image.sidecar.history.

assumptions: The colour table is taken as monotonic in intensity; nothing here says how.
The date is the label’s; no time within its minute is used.

validation.check: the frame holds one disc of about the expected size, centred: the pixels at 30 or above fill a disc whose equivalent radius is within the stated fraction of the width, with its centre within 2 percent of the middle

against.quantity: equivalent disc radius over the width
against.ref: the disc of the Sun fills about 92 percent of the width of the archive’s browse picture
